report:
Reviewed the complete callsite_updates claim, its single ordinary implementation association in compile/mod.rs, and its complete single ordinary annotated integration test. No TODO/N/A entries exist. Requirements are (1) author-written expectation locations survive compile_test!, (2) blessing changes the expectation at that call site rather than harness/generated fixture code, (3) ordinary comparison does not mutate source, and (4) updated expectations are verified in an independent later run with updates disabled.

Implementation inspection: compile_test! forwards each caller-provided expression directly into CompileTest setters. The expectation_field setters retain the original expect_test::Expect object; they do not recreate an expectation at a harness location. CompileTest::run calls assert_eq on those same retained objects after prepare succeeds, for observations, diagnostics, and queries. Consequently the library delegates comparison/update behavior to the caller's Expect and never relocates its source provenance. The temporary project in prepare receives fixture source only and is not used to construct expectation objects. All Sage implementation code essential to this location-preservation behavior is in the associated whole-file fragment.

Test adequacy: blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates contains its complete subprocess fixture and assertions visibly in the annotated function. Its disposable source contains compile_test! and an initially stale observation expectation. With updating disabled it requires an expectation failure and exact byte equality of the call-site source, establishing real comparison without mutation. With UPDATE_EXPECT=1 it requires success and reads the author-written src/lib.rs to assert the literal observation and u16 type appeared exactly once while the annotated fixture and empty diagnostics expectation remain present. An update mistakenly applied only to macro implementation or the separate compiler fixture could not satisfy those source checks and the subsequent successful compilation/comparison. A new cargo subprocess with UPDATE_EXPECT explicitly removed then must succeed and leave the blessed file byte-identical, satisfying independent verification. The earlier rustc-only unexpected-warning case also requires failure and byte-identical source even in update mode, consistent with validation preceding update. The three expectation fields share the same pass-through storage/assertion mechanism; the observation scenario exercises the source-location mechanism end to end while diagnostics remains visibly unchanged.

Captured additional source dependencies through review read: the complete integration-test file (including its Command import) and md/design/meta/reviews.md. There are no unrecorded workspace helper dependencies used in this assessment. Execution, separate from inspection: cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test callsite_updates passed (1 passed, 0 failed); existing compiler warnings were emitted. No Rust source changes were made. All claim aspects are accounted for and no edits are requested.
